purpose: Curated prospective-client questions to answer on snsco.in. Educational answers only (BCI Rule 36). Not yet researched or written. Source: legal-query-bank in firm profile/seo-deliverables.
answer_standard: Answer the question directly in the first paragraph, in general terms, as on a stated date
State the governing statute, forum, time limits and procedure; confirm every provision and case from two sources
Say plainly where the law is unsettled or differs by State
No call to contact the firm, no 'we can help', no fee or free-consultation language, no results or experience claims
No client stories, names or outcomes; hypotheticals labelled as such
Link to related guides, articles and the glossary; no comparisons with other lawyers

queue.query: How can a landlord evict a tenant in Kolkata under the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, and how is fair rent fixed?
queue.angle: Grounds of eviction, notice, Rent Controller, fair rent, deposit of rent, reasonable requirement, subletting, exclusions from the Act, appeals, execution; brief contrast with Delhi/UP rent laws (link existing guide)
queue.verify: West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act 1997 provisions on eviction and fair rent and its current status; Supreme Court / Calcutta HC authority on its operation; Transfer of Property Act Sec 106 notice

queue.query: How do I mutate a property in Kolkata, and how do I correct the record of rights in West Bengal?
queue.angle: Two systems: Kolkata Municipal Corporation assessment and mutation for urban property, and the Land and Land Reforms Department (banglarbhumi) mutation and record of rights elsewhere; documents, process, objections, appeals; mutation does not confer title (link existing mutation guides)
queue.verify: Kolkata Municipal Corporation Act 1980 assessment and mutation provisions; West Bengal Land Reforms Act 1955 mutation provisions; Supreme Court on mutation and title

queue.verify: RERA 2016 Sec 18, 31, 71; West Bengal RERA rules; Newtech Promoters (2021) SC; Supreme Court 2021 ruling on the West Bengal housing law and RERA
